answer: Charge every identity a refundable work-bond that only starts unlocking after several epochs of graded-passing answers, and slash it if two accounts share a signing pattern or answer-graph neighbor set. Because bonds sit illiquid on a public mesa until unlock, spinning a nebula of sockpuppets forces the attacker to lock capital per head for weeks. Bind admission to a single-use ivory computational proof so cloned keys cannot reuse the same ticket. The combination—capital lock, delayed franchise, and non-reusable proof—raises the cost of a fake majority above the expected reward.
